reasoning.summary: Index counter is strictly monotonic with no reset mechanism
reasoning.counterexample_evaluation: The counterexample in the audit map correctly identifies the pattern. Line 160 reads $.index, emits event with current value, then line 161 increments with ++$.index. This guarantees strict monotonicity.

guard_analysis.effectiveness: COMPLETE - uint256 cannot overflow in practice (2^256 transfers impossible)
COMPLETE - Searched for writes to $.index, only found ++$.index at line 161
COMPLETE - Transactions are processed sequentially, no parallel index emission possible

reasoning.invariant_check: For all transactions T1, T2 where T1 is mined before T2: index(T1) < index(T2). This follows from: (1) index starts at 0 or last saved value, (2) each _update increments by exactly 1, (3) no decrements or resets exist.
reasoning.formal_property: MONOTONIC(index): forall i,j. block_number(i) < block_number(j) => index(i) < index(j)

proof_trace.invariant_maintained: Index monotonically increases by 1 for each transfer

reviewed_items.title: Transfer completion atomicity (balance, hash chain, event)

reasoning.summary: All transfer operations execute atomically within single _update function
reasoning.counterexample_evaluation: The audit map counterexample correctly traces the atomicity. Lines 155-162 perform value check, balance update, hash chain update, event emission, and index increment in sequence within one function call. Any revert rolls back all.

guard_analysis.effectiveness: COMPLETE - All operations in single function, single transaction
COMPLETE - All state changes in a transaction either commit or revert together
COMPLETE - super._update() is internal, ShaHashChainLib.compute is pure, no callbacks

reasoning.invariant_check: For completed transfer: balance_updated AND hashChain_updated AND event_emitted. For reverted transfer: NONE of these occur. No partial state possible.
reasoning.formal_property: ATOMICITY: (balance_change => hashChain_change) AND (hashChain_change => event_emit) AND (event_emit => balance_change)

proof_trace.invariant_maintained: All operations complete together or none complete

reviewed_items.title: Transfer rejection precision at MAX_VALUE boundary

reasoning.summary: Boundary check uses <= comparison for precise MAX_VALUE enforcement
reasoning.counterexample_evaluation: The audit map analysis is accurate. Line 156 uses 'require(value <= type(uint248).max, ValueTooLarge())'. This means value == type(uint248).max passes (correct), value == type(uint248).max + 1 fails (correct).

guard_analysis.effectiveness: COMPLETE - Clear error for debugging, gas-efficient

reasoning.invariant_check: For all accepted values v: v <= 2^248 - 1. For all rejected values v: v > 2^248 - 1. No gap at boundary.
reasoning.formal_property: BOUNDARY: accepted(v) <=> v <= MAX_VALUE where MAX_VALUE = type(uint248).max

proof_trace.invariant_maintained: Value at exactly MAX_VALUE accepted, value above MAX_VALUE rejected

reviewed_items.title: Verifier contract stateless and always ready

reasoning.summary: Verifier has pause mechanism as intentional safety feature with owner-controlled recovery
reasoning.counterexample_evaluation: The audit map correctly identifies the two pause scenarios: (1) conflicting proofs trigger emergency at line 286, (2) owner calls activateEmergency() at line 458. Both are controlled scenarios. Recovery via deactivateEmergency() at line 464 exists.

guard_analysis.effectiveness: COMPLETE - Owner can restore normal operation
COMPLETE - Provides audit trail for pause cause

reasoning.invariant_check: Verifier can be paused only via: (1) conflicting proofs (indicates ZK bug - correct response), (2) owner action (trusted per model). Verifier can be unpaused via owner action. No permanent lock possible within trust model.

proof_trace.code_path: proveTransferRoot() with conflict -> _pause() -> [paused state] -> deactivateEmergency() -> _unpause() -> [normal state]
proof_trace.invariant_maintained: Pause is either intentional safety or owner action, both with recovery

reviewed_items.trust_model_note: Owner actions including pause/unpause are out of scope per trust assumptions. The 'NEEDS_VERIFICATION' in audit map is resolved as the pause mechanism is a feature, not a vulnerability.

reviewed_items.title: Hash chain checkpoint immutable once reserved

reasoning.summary: Reservation overwrites are idempotent due to deterministic zERC20 state
reasoning.counterexample_evaluation: The audit map identifies that reservedHashChains[index_] can be overwritten. However, the counterexample correctly concludes this is safe because: (1) index_ comes from zERC20.index() which is monotonic, (2) hashChain_ comes from zERC20.hashChain() which is deterministic for a given index. Same index = same hashChain = idempotent overwrite.

guard_analysis.effectiveness: COMPLETE - Index only increases, never decreases or resets
COMPLETE - hashChain is a pure function of all prior transfers
COMPLETE - Provides audit trail of reservations

reasoning.invariant_check: For reservedHashChains[i]: (1) first write sets value V from zERC20, (2) subsequent writes to same slot i can only occur if no transfers happened (same V), (3) after transfers, new index j > i is used. No slot can be overwritten with different value.
reasoning.formal_property: IDEMPOTENT: reservedHashChains[i] written multiple times => all writes have same value

proof_trace.code_path: reserveHashChain() -> index_ = token.index() -> hashChain_ = token.hashChain() -> reservedHashChains[index_] = hashChain_
proof_trace.invariant_maintained: Overwrite only possible with same value due to deterministic zERC20 state
edge_cases_checked: transfers between reservations (new index, new slot)
